thread:
sam_support: Heads-up — acme-inc reported recurring 502/504s from the Hosted API edge during a large embeddings workload around 09:12 UTC. They say it started after a spike in concurrent streams. Posting short repro and logs.

maya_eng: Thanks — can you paste the curl repro and any edge logs you have? Is this single region or cross-region?

sam_support: Repro they used (sanitized):
```
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer xxxxx\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"embed-large\",\"inputs\":[\"long text...\"],\"batch_size\":50}'
```
They also send multiple parallel curl jobs (~80 concurrent) from a single client.

sam_support: Edge logs (snippet):
```
[09:12:03] envoy [info] upstream reset: code=ENVOY_CONNECTION_... stream_reset reason=connection failure
[09:12:04] edge-proxy pool exhausted: keepalive_pools=0 inflight_streams=240
[09:12:05] auth-proxy 502 to tenant-router trace=trace-12345 header-inject failed \
```

leo_sre: Those logs smell like keepalive/connpool exhaustion + auth backend slow. Do we see h2 GOAWAY or RST_STREAM metrics around that window?

maya_eng: Pulling traces now. Preliminary: auth-token rotation happened at 09:11:50 (rolling), triggered a small auth cache miss storm. With ~80 concurrent embed streams per client, midproxy started opening many new connections and hit the per-worker connection cap. That caused queues and some stream resets -> 502s/504s.

clara_prod: Customer says they didn't change client behavior — the spike was an ingestion batch job that ramped faster than usual today. They got ~3k requests/minute for a 2m window.

sam_support: Repro steps we suggested to customer: 1) throttle concurrency to 16-32 streams, 2) retry with exponential backoff on 502/504, 3) switch to smaller batch_size for embeddings. They confirmed mitigations reduced errors.

leo_sre: Quick mitigations we applied: temporarily increased edge keepalive timeout from 30s -> 90s for the affected fleet and raised per-worker connection cap by 25% for the midproxy pool. Also disabled auth header rewrite for tenant-router for the window to avoid extra auth roundtrips.

maya_eng: Follow-up notes: Root cause = combination of auth token rotation causing auth cache misses + sudden parallel embedding streams causing h2 connpool thrash. Envoy started creating new HTTP/2 streams on new connections faster than upstream could accept, leading to RST/GOAWAY.

sam_support: Customer happy with mitigation but wants long-term fix. They asked if we can provide SLA credits and a postmortem.

leo_sre: Action items:
- (maya) add guardrail that staggers auth rotations when client concurrency > X (experiment).
- (eng-runtime) improve backpressure handling for large batch embedding routes (batching + pre-queue).
- (sre) add alert when auth cache miss rate spikes > 5% for >1m.
- (support) coordinate credit request with finance for acme-inc.

maya_eng: Also adding a short-term rule: for /v1/embeddings route, cap max concurrent streams per client IP to 48 to avoid single-tenant thrash. We'll ship rule as a config flag behind a fail-open switch.

envoy-bot: Deploy 3287654400: edge-keepalive/connpool-tune rolled to prod (canary 10%).

clara_prod: Customer noted one more thing — when they retried immediately, they saw a different error: 502 with upstream \"auth-503\" in header. Probably auth backend overload.

leo_sre: Good catch — we should add circuit-breaker on auth path so auth backpressure doesn't cascade to edge.

sam_support: I'll collect timeline + customer repro and start a support ticket for credits + PM for postmortem. Tagging @maya_eng @leo_sre for the follow-ups. :thumbsup:

maya_eng: Sounds good. I'll start a follow-up PR for the client concurrency cap and add a regression test that simulates token rotation during large parallel embed batches.

sam_support: Closing loop here once postmortem draft is ready. Thanks everyone.
